subject: binary-order
requirement: Evaluate ordinary operands left to right exactly once, including owned Bytes operands.

subject: call-order
requirement: Evaluate receiver then positional arguments once; native hidden-result storage preserves effects and caller ownership.

subject: aggregate-order
requirement: List arguments and named product fields evaluate in lexical source order, independent of storage field order.

subject: short-circuit
requirement: && and its exact alias ∧, and || and its exact alias ∨, evaluate the right operand only when required. The English words and/or/not are not executable aliases in Edition 1.

subject: temporary-lifetime
requirement: Temporaries remain valid through use, and independent returned owned values do not alias.

subject: discard-and-return
requirement: Discard keeps effects; return suppresses subsequent control paths and runs required cleanup.

subject: builtin-types
requirement: Bool, Int64, binary64 Float, Unicode Char, UTF-8 Text and Bytes retain distinct typed identities.

subject: inference-and-binding
requirement: Direct inference and explicit one-shot initialization agree; assignment preserves type and mutability.

subject: no-coercions
requirement: No implicit Bool/Int/Float/Char/Text conversion at binding boundaries; rejected initializer retains causal type error.

subject: nominal-identity
requirement: Alias layout equals referent layout; newtype requires explicit construction/unwrap; enum discriminants and active payloads remain distinct.

subject: generic-constraints
requirement: Supported scalar generic constraints are checked, not erased; const arguments specialize independently.

subject: overload-ranking
requirement: Exact supported receiver/argument types select deterministically regardless of declaration order. Named/default calls retain their bounded pure profile.

subject: explicit-conversions
requirement: Narrowing, textual parsing and numeric rounding use explicit operations with checked domain/error behavior.

subject: move
requirement: Move transfers ownership exactly once and invalidates the old binding.

subject: copy-clone
requirement: Value copies and explicit owned clones remain independent; clone allocation is accounted and released.

subject: borrow-aliasing
requirement: Shared/unique views constrain mutation, reset, drop and move until release.

subject: lifetime-escape
requirement: Borrow cannot escape its owner; function result ownership is explicit and caller-owned.

subject: cleanup
requirement: Success, early return and allocation failure release all live resources exactly once.

subject: layout-ownership
requirement: Distinct live owned values must remain independent and valid through their permitted lifetimes. Internal descriptor offsets and generation representation are not language syntax.

subject: effect-lattice
requirement: Effect tracking is a compiler contract, not a public constructor or a promise that its internal bit layout is a language type. Public effectful calls remain subject to declared purity and authority.

subject: source-effect-inference
requirement: Interpolation permits only pure expressions, including transitive callees; discarded effects still execute outside pure contexts.

subject: capability-grants
requirement: Imports grant no authority. Only host-authenticated, scoped capabilities authorize their corresponding sinks; attenuation cannot amplify the grant. The native grant representation is not public syntax.

subject: import-no-grant
requirement: Import and prelude resolution grant no capabilities and execute no user initializer.

subject: policy-before-sink
requirement: An operation denied by the admitted capability policy must fail before its sink; a failed authorization must not consume the capability budget. Internal policy request layouts are not public constructors.

subject: privacy-and-trust
requirement: Sensitive input must follow the admitted redaction and flow policy; it must not appear in a redacted sink. Native Sensitive/Trusted metadata does not declare additional public source constructors.

subject: provenance
requirement: Provenance metadata must preserve authenticated source/transform relationships when that tooling contract is used. Metadata lineage does not add a source-language provenance constructor.

subject: option-layout
requirement: Option has distinct Some(payload) and None() variants. Some carries the declared payload type; None carries no payload. Only the selected variant is observed; invalid payloads and wrong observers reject.

subject: result-layout
requirement: Ok/Err preserve distinct success/error types and owned payloads across function returns.

subject: fallback-laziness
requirement: unwrapOr(value) evaluates its value argument eagerly. The admitted ?? and combinator profiles select the active variant; this does not admit arbitrary effectful callback forms.

subject: error-identity
requirement: Error code/category/span/context and cause remain structured; messages are derived from active error identity and caller context.

subject: match
requirement: Current enum matching observes only the selected active variant and rejects invalid patterns according to the finite source profile.

subject: propagation
requirement: ? retains the enclosing supported Result type and propagates the active error without reusing helper status as payload.

subject: module-init-order
requirement: The native module graph orders dependencies before consumers and lists each module once, independently of unit argument order. The admitted pure source/interface profile has zero runtime user initializers. Native initializer/rollback tests supplement this boundary without granting effectful imported startup.

subject: module-init-failure
requirement: Cycles and effectful imported startup reject before publication. Native rollback reverses successfully initialized resources in the internal initialization contract; interface loading executes no user code.

subject: pure-constants
requirement: Pure source/interface constants preserve values and typed symbol identity. Interface loading is not execution.

subject: tasks-futures
requirement: Within the separately measured material profile, without stable-availability promotion: Supported noncapturing task callbacks execute once; Future is single-consumer and map preserves effects.

subject: channels
requirement: Within the separately measured material profile, without stable-availability promotion: Bounded FIFO transport preserves values, capacity errors and close behavior; source loops compose with independent random states.

subject: cancellation-scheduling
requirement: Within the separately measured material profile, without stable-availability promotion: Cancellation blocks admission; deterministic scheduler/select order is bounded, not a promise of preemptive async source.

subject: resource-closure
requirement: Private filesystem operations enforce beneath/no-symlink paths and close resources. Native synchronization semantics are a separate internal supplement and do not grant additional stable source APIs.

subject: allocation-budget
requirement: System blocks <=65536 bytes, arena capacity <=1048576; OOM releases earlier successful allocations without publishing a later sink.

subject: arithmetic-failures
requirement: Checked integer overflow/division traps do not wrap silently; explicit status preserves canonical return semantics.

subject: output-capacity
requirement: Tagged publication budget 32 and error text pool 4096 are checked before artifacts/output; plus-one rejects.

subject: recursion-budget
requirement: At most 64 active supported call frames; depth-boundary programs terminate with a defined trap, never hang.

subject: publication-atomicity
requirement: Failure before an atomic sink preserves existing files; rename/capacity/parser failures leave no partial output.

subject: source-encoding
requirement: Source must be valid UTF-8. Invalid sequences, executable bidi controls and confusable spellings reject; byte offsets are measured in the original bytes. Formatting must preserve literal and comment payloads.

subject: identifier-identity
requirement: Identifiers use ASCII letters/underscore and subsequent ASCII digits as admitted by the lexical token owner; exact spelling is significant. No Unicode normalization or confusable substitution is implicit; keyword boundaries remain distinct.

subject: maximal-munch
requirement: The longest registered token in its admitted context is consumed; compound Unicode tokens retain their whole UTF-8 spans. Recognition alone does not activate a reserved grammar form.

subject: comments
requirement: Line comments continue to line end. Block comments nest to depth 64 inclusive; depth 65 rejects without an artifact. Comments cannot activate executable statements. A doc block is structured syntax, not trivia.

subject: literal-payload
requirement: Radix/separator integer spellings preserve their values. Float is binary64, Char is one Unicode scalar, Text retains decoded UTF-8 bytes; raw and multiline forms preserve their respective escape and newline rules.

subject: precedence-associativity
requirement: The registered binding powers and associativity govern grouping: power is right associative and binds more strongly than unary minus; parentheses explicitly override grouping.

subject: imports-and-capsules
requirement: Simple and selective imports have explicit aliases; named/anonymous capsules and reexports preserve logical module/export identity. Resolution must not depend on a fixture filename. Imported pure interfaces execute no initializer.

subject: material-interface
requirement: The admitted source-facing binary .ni profile supplies public Int constants with original symbol/type identity; a metadata-only interface cannot manufacture an executable value. Provider-source and material-interface consumers must agree.

subject: doc-attachment
requirement: A doc block attaches to a material declaration through native AST/DocRecord identity. Its examples and laws are actual Nebo programs. Textual registry identities and serialized SymbolIds must not be conflated.

subject: text-units
requirement: UTF-8 byte length, Unicode scalar count and grapheme segmentation are distinct operations. Each operation must obey its declared unit and boundary behavior; no implicit normalization is performed.

subject: format-and-render
requirement: Format/interpolation arguments retain lexical evaluation and typed domain checks. Admitted FormatPlan/RenderPlan profiles preserve exact text and node effects; interpolation expressions must be pure.

subject: console-and-scan
requirement: console() is the canonical output surface; print is not valid Nebo. Mock/stdin Scan follows its typed result, cancellation, bounds and redaction contracts. Headless/software evidence does not assert live desktop or hardware availability.

subject: diagnostic-contract
requirement: Invalid source must reject before executable publication. Diagnostic code, severity, phase and half-open UTF-8 byte spans are contractual; JSON-lines schema 1 and SARIF/LSP projections preserve that identity. LSP positions use UTF-16.

subject: diagnostic-options
requirement: The public check command forwards bounded --max-errors (1..64), exclusive --fail-fast/--keep-going, human/short --show-fixes and --path-style relative/workspace/absolute to the native diagnostic owner. Duplicated options, incompatible modes and out-of-range arguments reject as usage errors before artifact publication.

subject: process-status
requirement: The supported Linux process interface observes the low byte of the explicit integer return. Signal termination is distinct from an ordinary exit; a mathematical intermediate must not replace the return.

subject: edition-and-compatibility
requirement: Edition 1 specifies the admitted bounded profile. The current selector also accepts Edition 2 for compatible forms; unknown IDs reject. Neither selector nor migration preview activates a reserved form or changes files.

subject: declared-target-and-limits
requirement: Executable conformance here is x86_64 Linux System V ELF. Other targets and wider profiles acquire no guarantee by name. Public bounds and failure policies are enumerated in IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED-REGISTRY.tsv; compiler and test-harness budgets are distinguished.

subject: conformance-and-consumption
requirement: Every admitted source statement must be accounted for exactly once. Changed values govern observations; missing rules, unclassified current declarations, dropped statements and altered oracles cannot close conformance.
